findings.summary: WithValidMethods with an empty slice is ignored, so a computed-empty allowlist restricts nothing
findings.description:
## Summary

`jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{})` should permit nothing. The port treats an empty slice as "option not set" and applies **no** algorithm restriction at all, accepting for example an `HS256` token. Upstream rejects everything for `algorithms: []`.

Parity case: **`alg-allowlist-empty`** (group `algorithms`).

## Upstream vs port behaviour

| | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `jwt.verify(tok, secret, {algorithms: []})` | **rejects** — `options.algorithms.indexOf(alg) === -1` holds for every `alg`, so `invalid algorithm` |
| `jwt.Parse(tok, keyfunc, jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{}))` | **accepts** |

## Impact

Fails open, and silently. Allowlists are frequently *computed*: from config, from an environment variable split on commas, from a JWKS `alg` field, or from an intersection of "what this tenant permits" with "what this deployment supports". Any of those can produce an empty list — a missing env var, a typo, a tenant with no algorithms configured, an empty intersection. The caller's code reads as "restrict to exactly this set"; the effect is "impose no restriction", i.e. accept every registered algorithm — precisely the state that makes the algorithm-confusion issue (tracked separately) reachable.

Rated **moderate**: on its own it does not accept any token the library would not accept with no allowlist argument at all, and it requires the application to compute an empty allowlist. Its severity comes from being the silent enabler of the algorithm-confusion path rather than from direct exploitation.

## Root cause

`parser.go`:

```go
if len(p.validAlgs) > 0 && !contains(p.validAlgs, alg) {   // parser.go:183
    return token, fmt.Errorf("%w: alg %q is not accepted", ErrSignatureInvalid, alg)
}
```

`len(p.validAlgs) > 0` conflates "no allowlist configured" with "an allowlist that permits nothing".

## Reproduction

Token: `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJleHAiOjE3MDAwMDM2MDAsImlhdCI6MTcwMDAwMDAwMH0.uSyiX6mW2QalXyp6PI6h2UsPl323b6Mz8hggXGyW0rw`, HMAC secret `parity-hmac-secret-256-bits-long-enough`.

```go
tok, err := jwt.Parse(token, keyfunc,
    jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{}),
    jwt.WithTimeFunc(func() time.Time { return time.Unix(1700000100, 0) }))
// err == nil - the empty allowlist imposed nothing
```

## Suggested fix

Track "was the option supplied" separately from the slice length — e.g. a `validAlgsSet bool`, or have `WithValidMethods` store a non-nil empty slice and test `p.validAlgs != nil`. An empty allowlist must reject every token.

## Affected version

`github.com/malcolmston/jwt` at `v0.3.0` (published module). No published version contains a fix.

## Evidence / provenance

- Parity suite `parity/jwt` (`GOWORK=off go test ./parity/jwt/`), upstream pinned to `jsonwebtoken@9.0.2` (auth0/node-jsonwebtoken).
- Case parity ~92.8%; this case is listed in `parity/jwt/parity.json` under `mismatchedCases` and is not one of the 3 declared deviations.
- All verification cases pin the clock (`clockTimestamp` upstream, `jwt.WithTimeFunc` in the port), so nothing here depends on wall time.

findings.summary: Algorithm confusion: HS256 token signed with an RSA public-key PEM is accepted when no allowlist is set
findings.description:
## Summary

The classic algorithm-confusion attack. An attacker takes the RSA **public** key PEM a service publishes, uses its raw bytes as an HMAC secret, and signs an `{"alg":"HS256"}` token. A verifier that hands `jwt.Parse` those PEM bytes from its `Keyfunc` and passes **no** algorithm allowlist accepts the forged token. Upstream `jsonwebtoken@9.0.2` rejects it.

Parity case: **`alg-confusion-hs-token-pem-secret-no-allowlist`** (group `algorithms`).

## Upstream vs port behaviour

Upstream `verify.js` calls `crypto.createPublicKey(secretOrPublicKey)`; when that succeeds it *sets* `options.algorithms` to the RSA/PSS set, so an `HS256` header can never match. The port performs no such inference: with no `WithValidMethods`, any registered `alg` in the header is honoured and `SigningMethodHMAC` accepts whatever `[]byte` it is handed.

| | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `jwt.verify(tok, pubPem, {})` | **rejects** — `JsonWebTokenError: invalid algorithm` |
| `jwt.Parse(tok, func(*jwt.Token) (any, error) { return pemBytes, nil })` | **accepts**, claims `{"sub":"attacker","iat":1700000000,"exp":1700003600}` |

## Impact

The RSA public key is by definition public — served from a JWKS endpoint or committed as a `.pem`. An attacker who can read it can mint tokens with arbitrary `sub`, roles and `exp` and have them accepted as genuine: full authentication bypass for an affected service.

Rated **high**, not critical, because two application-side preconditions must both hold: the caller passes **no** `WithValidMethods` allowlist, *and* the `Keyfunc` returns raw key material as `[]byte` rather than a typed key. Both mitigations are confirmed working by adjacent parity cases, so this is a missing safety inference rather than a broken cryptographic primitive:

- `alg-confusion-hs-token-rs-allowlist` — with `jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"RS256"})`, both libraries reject.
- `alg-confusion-hs-token-rsa-pubkey-no-allowlist` — returning a typed `*rsa.PublicKey` from the `Keyfunc`, both reject (the port via `ErrInvalidKeyType`).

Note that the naive one-to-one port of `jwt.verify(tok, pubPem)` produces exactly the vulnerable shape, and upstream silently protected that caller.

## Reproduction

Forged token (HMAC key = the literal bytes of `parity/jwt/keys/rsa-2048.pub.pem`):

```
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJleHAiOjE3MDAwMDM2MDAsImlhdCI6MTcwMDAwMDAwMCwic3ViIjoiYXR0YWNrZXIifQ.AlobPGdy1Vq7VLsN2P9oz3DC0phkPddsglG5gC1Oxi4
```

```go
pem, _ := os.ReadFile("rsa-2048.pub.pem")
tok, err := jwt.Parse(forged, func(*jwt.Token) (any, error) { return pem, nil },
    jwt.WithTimeFunc(func() time.Time { return time.Unix(1700000100, 0) }))
// err == nil, tok.Claims["sub"] == "attacker"
```

## Suggested fix

Infer an algorithm restriction from the key material when no allowlist was given: if the `Keyfunc` returns bytes that parse as a PEM/DER public or private key, restrict the acceptable `alg` set to the matching asymmetric family and refuse `HS*`. At minimum, refuse a `[]byte` key beginning with `-----BEGIN` and document that `WithValidMethods` is mandatory.

## Affected version

`github.com/malcolmston/jwt` at `v0.3.0` (published module). No published version contains a fix.

## Evidence / provenance

- Parity suite `parity/jwt` (`GOWORK=off go test ./parity/jwt/`), upstream pinned to `jsonwebtoken@9.0.2` (auth0/node-jsonwebtoken).
- Case parity ~92.8%; this case is listed in `parity/jwt/parity.json` under `mismatchedCases` and is not one of the 3 declared deviations.
- All verification cases pin the clock (`clockTimestamp` upstream, `jwt.WithTimeFunc` in the port), so nothing here depends on wall time.
